newsitem.title: UK: UK reviewing aid to Kenya after crackdown.
newsitem.headline: UK reviewing aid to Kenya after crackdown.

text.p: Britain said on Wednesday it would reduce its aid to Kenya if the Nairobi government continued to crack down on demands for constitutional change.
At least nine people were killed across Kenya on July 7 after police moved in to stop pro-reform rallies.
International Development Secretary (minister) Clare Short told parliament she was concerned by the repression and said Britain was already reviewing the aid it provided to Kenya.
British aid to the former colony, which won independence in 1963, worth 28 million pounds ($47 million) in the 1995/96 financial year.
"It would be a tragedy if Kenya were to become more and more repressive and cut off from the rest of the world," Short said.
"But we cannot tolerate the kind of behaviour that's continuing, and continue to give the sort of contribution in aid donations that Britain has historically given to Kenya," she said.
